records.reason: Measure m177 at 5/1 and 50 ul between the measured 2/1 and 50/1 conditions, probing where the anomalous V2 tail begins. This directly extends the unresolved m177 surface seen in 4862e2fb71344ce16021, b514312eda7950cdcf1c, and 5b706e17e8412d02342f.
Measure m177 at 2/1 and 100 ul between the measured 2/1, 50 ul and 150 ul points. It isolates loading interpolation in a region where V2 differs sharply across nearby records.
The pure-EA m177 point at 50 ul complements the measured pure-EA 150 ul anchor 4466eabae9624380fbc6 and tests whether the high-ratio tail is suppressed at the strong-solvent endpoint.
Measure m80 at 2/1 and 100 ul to extend the nearly flat measured 10/1-to-50/1 response at 150 ul. This tests whether saturation begins at lower ratio than the model suggests.
The m80 1/1, 150 ul point provides a lower-ratio anchor at the same loading as the measured 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 points, separating a genuine plateau from an unlearned transition.
Measure m80 at 50/1 and 50 ul against the measured 50/1, 150 ul result. This is a focused loading contrast for a family whose ratio response is already observed to be weak.
A diphenyl sulfone anchor at 2/1 and 50 ul adds a highly polarizable, donor-free aromatic structure in a moderate-retention region, testing transfer beyond the common carbonyl and ester families.
The 50/1 m162 nitrile-bromide condition probes a late mobile-phase endpoint for a compact halogenated acceptor-rich aromatic, supplying structure-conditioned high-ratio supervision.

Measure brominated methoxybenzyl m112 at 50/1 with an intermediate loading-solvent volume. It tests whether ether placement and benzylic bromide connectivity alter the high-ratio response of aromatic ethers.
The pure-EA m12 point supplies a strong-solvent endpoint for a hydrocarbon scaffold, helping calibrate the lower-retention floor across nonpolar molecules and loading conditions.
Measure carbonyl-rich m94 at 20/1 and 150 ul to add a late-ratio neutral multifunctional ester and test whether its finish follows the broader carbonyl-family response.

The m184 2/1, 50 ul dibromobenzaldehyde condition covers a halogenated aldehyde at moderate ratio and low loading, testing transfer of aromaticity and acceptor effects without relying on high predicted volume.
This m24 1/1, 50 ul hydrocarbon point adds a low-polarity aliphatic aromatic structure and helps distinguish mobile-phase effects from heteroatom-driven retention.

Measure phenylbutanol m67 at 2/1 and 150 ul to extend alcohol-family coverage in a moderate condition. It tests whether an accessible donor produces a distinct onset and finish relative to non-donor analogues.
The m99 2/1, 1000 ul condition is a high loading-solvent-volume probe for an alpha-hydroxy ester, useful for testing loading and donor accessibility in a polar small molecule.
Measure hydrophobic m50 at 20/1 and 150 ul to provide a late-ratio anchor for a donor-free alkyl arene and broaden coverage of ordinary low-polarity retention.
The m164 20/1 condition probes a conjugated bis-enone-like aromatic structure in a high-ratio regime, testing whether extended pi-systems receive an excessive or insufficient solvent correction.
A bulky brominated polyaromatic m0 at pure EA adds a sterically shielded, donor-free structure at the strong-solvent endpoint and tests the lower-volume boundary for hydrophobic compounds.
The m100 1/1, 100 ul tert-butyl benzoate point adds an ester-substituted aromatic with a bulky hydrophobe, testing whether steric accessibility changes transfer from simpler benzoates.

Measure benzil-like m168 at 20/1 and 100 ul. The observed m168 record e82a87ee526fdd9b1e8d shows a broad finish in a related late condition, so this label helps supervise both heads in a diketone family.
The matched m99 1/1, 1000 ul point pairs with selected m99 at 2/1 and fixed loading-solvent volume, supplying a local ratio response for a polar hydroxy ester.
The simple acetophenone m42 50/1 condition adds a compact, donor-free ketone at a weak mobile phase, testing whether high-ratio growth transfers from larger aromatic ketones.
Measure aldehyde m183 at 5/1 and 100 ul to add a flexible phenylalkyl carbonyl in a moderate ratio region, contrasting constrained and heteroatom-rich carbonyl families.
The m102 2/1 methyl chlorobenzoate condition provides a compact halogenated ester anchor at moderate ratio, testing connectivity and halogen effects separately from aminobenzoates.
The m50 1/1 and selected 20/1 points form a same-molecule ratio pair at 150 ul, giving a useful slope estimate for a low-polarity structure.
Measure m91 at 20/1 and 50 ul, an electron-poor multifunctional ester with an unusual predicted response. It tests a chemically distinct condition surface at low loading.
The m101 condition uses a nonstandard 68 ul sample volume and 200 ul loading-solvent volume, adding coverage of irregular loading contexts that are otherwise easy for the model to smooth away.
Measure stilbene-like m14 at 5/1 and 50 ul as a donor-free aromatic baseline. Together with the selected m14 high-ratio point, it tests retention change across mobile-phase strength.
The m16 5/1, 150 ul acrylate point adds a flexible hydrophobic ester at higher loading and can be compared with the selected high-ratio m16 condition for loading-response transfer.
Measure m168 at pure EA and 50 ul to complement the selected 20/1 point and the observed late m168 condition e82a87ee526fdd9b1e8d, separating solvent response from tail behavior.
The m156 2/1 fluorinated hydrocarbon point covers a highly halogenated, donor-free scaffold at moderate ratio and tests transfer in a sparse nonpolar region.
The m52 5/1, 150 ul condition adds a compact brominated alkene at substantial loading, supplying a low-polarity condition anchor distinct from aromatic carbonyls.

hypotheses.content: m177 has a strongly nonlinear ratio and loading surface, especially for V2; the late 50/1 tail is not explained by a smooth monotone loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A smooth global solvent or loading correction could spread the m177 tail to neighboring rows and damage V2 accuracy. Local labels can teach whether the discontinuity is molecule-specific, loading-specific, or a rare recorded regime.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At intermediate ratios and loadings, where does m177 V2 leave the low-tail regime, and does the departure occur in V1, V2, or both?

hypotheses.content: m80 has a largely saturated ratio response over the measured 10/1-to-50/1 range at 150 ul, so the model's projected increase is too steep for this neutral diester family.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Additional labels around the flat curve can suppress an incorrect global ratio slope and improve calibration for ordinary neutral multifunctional esters.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m80 plateau extend to 1/1 and 2/1, and is it preserved when loading changes from 150 to 50 or 100 ul?

hypotheses.content: Loading and mobile-phase responses are family-specific, and V1 and V2 can change independently; broad descriptor pooling is insufficient in several structural regions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Paired condition and loading labels can improve transfer across the Row-distribution while preventing interval width from acting as a substitute for either target.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural families preserve an onset shift with nearly fixed V2, and which show coupled changes in both heads?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback confirms that m177 at 50/1 and 50 ul has a late measured V2 of 59.88 mL, while nearby 50/1 measurements at 100 and 150 ul are 7.31 and 81.30 mL. The m177 discontinuity therefore remains unresolved and merits additional local conditions. In contrast, m80 measurements at 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 with 150 ul remain near 5 to 8 mL, weakening the earlier steep-response interpretation for that family. The m146 midpoint was close to prediction, supporting an onset-specific loading effect, while m120, m107, m90, m141, m208, and other recent outcomes reinforce that large errors cluster in particular structural families and can affect V1 and V2 differently.
batch_rationale: The batch begins with six targeted m177 and m80 measurements that discriminate the strongest unresolved nonlinear and saturation hypotheses. The remaining points provide broad, chemically meaningful coverage of high-ratio endpoints, pure-EA anchors, moderate-ratio interpolation, unusual loading contexts, halogenated aromatics, carbonyl-rich compounds, esters, ethers, hydrocarbons, and flexible aldehydes. Same-molecule ratio and loading contrasts are included for m99, m50, m14, m16, and m168, while the rest add structural-condition anchors that improve transfer into sparsely represented regions. This combination should repair local failure surfaces while giving the retrained model reusable supervision across the Row-distribution.
